codeReview.summary: The commit correctly adds a 30-second timeout to the thread.join() call in _run_coroutine_sync, logs a warning when the thread fails to finish, and raises TimeoutError. The worker correctly identified that the TypeVar generic return type and the DYNAMIC_ANALYSIS handler stub were already present from the prior async-pipeline-executor feature and focused on the missing timeout behavior. Two well-structured tests were added: one covering the DYNAMIC_ANALYSIS stub handler output, and one verifying the timeout/warning/exception path using a FakeThread monkeypatch. All 4 tests in the file pass. The constant SYNC_COROUTINE_THREAD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is module-level and clearly named. No bugs or edge cases were missed.

issues.description: After TimeoutError is raised the daemon thread is still running in the background. This is acceptable for a sync fallback path (the caller will propagate the error), but a comment noting the thread leak would improve clarity for future maintainers.

summary: PASS. The implementation correctly addresses the thread.join() timeout requirement (30s with warning and TimeoutError). The TypeVar annotation and DYNAMIC_ANALYSIS handler were pre-existing from the async-pipeline-executor feature — the worker correctly identified this and focused on the actual gap. Tests are thorough: one exercises the dynamic analysis stub end-to-end through the pipeline, the other verifies the timeout/warning/raise path via monkeypatching. All 4 tests pass. One non-blocking observation: the daemon thread leaks after timeout, which is acceptable but could use a comment.
